Get started

#Bots

Disband bots are self-hosted integrations. You run the code, Disband relays messages to and from it. Disband never hosts or executes your bot's code.

#How it works

  1. Create a bot in Settings → Bots (or the Developers portal) and pick the scopes it needs. You get a token back — it is shown once.
  2. Generate an invite link — targeted to a specific server, or a general invite that anyone can use (the recipient picks the server).
  3. The server owner (or a channel manager) opens the link and approves. The bot becomes a member of the server.
  4. You run one of the client libraries somewhere (a server, a cloud function, your laptop) and it connects to Disband with the token.

#Scopes

A bot's reach in a server is the intersection of the scopes you requested when creating it and the scopes the owner approved for that specific server:

Scope Description
messages.read Receive message events and read messages, channels, categories, and pins.
messages.write Send and edit messages, and pin messages.
messages.delete Delete and bulk-delete messages, and unpin messages.
messages.react Add and remove the bot's reactions.
members.read List members, read member detail, and list roles.
members.kick Kick members.
members.ban Ban, unban, and list bans.
members.timeout Time out members.
channels.read List channels and categories, read channel detail and overwrites.
channels.manage Create, rename, reorder, and delete channels and categories — also needs the manage_channels role in the server.
webhooks.manage Create, edit, and delete webhooks — also needs manage_webhooks.
roles.manage Create, edit, and delete roles; assign roles; set channel overwrites — also needs manage_roles.
servers.read Read a space's name, description, icon, banner, and member count.
audit.read Read the audit log (or hold the view_audit_log role permission).

Management scopes are a second gate, not a replacement for role permissions. Bots still need the matching role in the space — for example, channels.manage plus manage_channels. Private channels are implemented with channel permission overwrites; see Extended API and private channels.

#Token authentication

Every API call is authenticated with the bot token:

Authorization: Bot <token>

Bot tokens are hashed at rest — the raw token is never stored or retrievable. If it leaks (or you no longer need the bot), revoke it in Settings → Bots; revocation kills the token immediately.

#Customizing your bot

Bots can be customized from the Developers portal (/developers/applications):

  • Name — the display name shown in the member list and on messages.
  • Avatar — profile picture URL (any HTTPS image).
  • Banner — banner image URL for the bot's profile.
  • Bio — a short description shown on the bot's profile.
  • Scopes — add or remove scopes at any time (existing grants are not affected until a new invite is approved).

#General invite links

When creating an invite, enable General invite to generate a link that anyone can use. The recipient signs in to Disband, picks a space they manage, and approves the bot there. Great for distributing bots publicly or in documentation.

Targeted invites (the default) lock the invite to a specific server and require the bot owner to be a member of that server.

#Limits & safety

  • Up to 5 bots per account. A bot can be revoked at any time, which kills its token.
  • Messages up to 4,000 characters. Bots need the mention_everyone role permission to use @everyone.
  • Only a server's owner or a channel manager can approve a bot invite. Invites expire after 7 days.
  • Bot tokens are hashed at rest; the raw token is never stored or retrievable.
  • Bots can never reach the database directly — every action goes through scoped API endpoints.
  • Rate limits apply per bot token. If you hit 429, honor Retry-After.

#Install the clients

Shell
# JavaScript / TypeScript
npm install @disband/bot

# Python
pip install disband-bot

No zip downloads — install directly from npm and PyPI.
